sections.title: étel: the general word for food
sections.content: étel means "food" or "a dish" in general — the word you reach for when you're not naming one specific thing. Combine it with eszik/iszik and the accusative -t you already know from A1 to talk about food in general terms: some food, any food, food as a category, not one particular plate.

items.english: I eat a lot of food daily.
What kind of food do you like most?
I mostly eat soup and salad.

sections.content: eszem, eszel, eszik... in these examples is the plain, indefinite form you just learned — sok ételt, levest, and salátát are all general objects ("some food", "soup", not "the soup"), so the verb stays in its ordinary shape. Hold onto that thought: later in this unit you'll meet what changes when the object becomes one specific, known thing instead.
